[autotest] Make sure autotest is staged before package install Fixing an issue where at times the package manager would attempt to install autotest after devserver's cache had expired. The install would fail silently and would blow up when the packages.checksum was a devserver 404 page instead of the expected checksum file format. Simply use the cros_host.verify_job_repo_url function to verify the devserver is reachable, and make the devserver stage the autotest artifacts if needed. updater5: Fix FAFT firmware_UpdateFirmwareDataKeyVersion test In FAFT, the system will try to update firmware with different keys, and will want to update even if the key version will trigger firmware anti-rollback detection. In FAFT this is did explicitly by passing --nocheck_keys into firmware updater. The updater5 (futility based updater) did not support --nocheck_keys. Instead the key "for new RO and RW" is always checked. The --force can skip TPM key checks. So, if we need to map --nocheck_keys to new updater, it should be --force. This change looks at --nocheck_keys and --force, and will add a --force when invoking "futility update". BUG=b:111403731 TEST=emerge-$BOARD chromeos-firmware-$BOARD chromeos-firmwareupdate --nocheck_keys # --force applied Change-Id: I2f6f832ed9c2152507c2cd86c4848b93b10d6246 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1249402 Commit-Ready: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org> Tested-by: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Wai-Hong Tam <waihong@google.com>

sys_util: add PUNCH_HOLE fallback for write_zeroes Some filesystems do not support FALLOC_FL_ZERO_RANGE; in particular, encrypted files on ext4 fail this request with -EOPNOTSUPP. Add a fallback to try fallocate with FALLOC_FL_PUNCH_HOLE before totally giving up and falling back to a regular write(). This should be more efficient for filesystems that support hole punching. BUG=None TEST=strace crosvm using qcow files on encrypted ext4 and verify that fallocate(FALLOC_FL_PUNCH_HOLE) is issued when required. Change-Id: Idffabc75ea0e1153efbb13cec8b4a25570427235 Signed-off-by: Daniel Verkamp <dverkamp@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1250022 Reviewed-by: Stephen Barber <smbarber@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dylan Reid <dgreid@chromium.org>

metrics: memd: fix panic processing Unlike log!(), warn!(), etc., panic messages (either from explicit calls to panic!() or implicitly, for instance through expect() calls) go to stderr instead of being routed through the log crate. Here we change all relevant expect() calls to unwrap_or_else(die!()) to produce output to both places. The relevant calls are those in the daemon proper, the unit tests don't matter. We also add futex() and exit_group() to the seccomp white list, since those calls are used when panicking. Additionally we add debug=true to [profile.release] to produce more symbols (see crbug.com/889991) to help analyze stack traces. These changes make memd exit with an error code instead of crashing. This does not create a crash report directly. However, init crashes are already reported via the anomaly collector, so we can monitor memd crashes in this fashion. In any case the crash report does not contain the panic message, and the stack trace is not particularly useful here since most errors are propagated back to the main loop. BUG=chromium:888630 TEST=tested on workstation and on device, with and without minijail Change-Id: I1430c43fbf9fc226ce2de7c9e3fdf966ff95688f Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1246240 Commit-Ready: Luigi Semenzato <semenzato@chromium.org> Tested-by: Luigi Semenzato <semenzato@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sonny Rao <sonnyrao@chromium.org>
